summary: Ferdinand von Eckstein (1790–1861) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer from circa 1810 to 1812 and was a member of the Société Asiatique from circa 1822 to 1861.
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Nalanda University and completed doctoral work supervised by Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola (1915–2017) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, having studied at the National University of San Marcos (~1933–1945). He held posts at the University of Buenos Aires (~1969) and directed the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (~1989–2017).
Fifth Karma Kuchen (born 1970) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under Penor Rinpoche as his heart son and succeeded him in 2000.
Filippo De Filippi (1869–1938) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.

Filippo Marsili is a scholar in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, and Arcangela Santoro, and later held a post at Saint Louis University.

Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate from Harvard University in 2015. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Yale (2017–2018) and a visiting assistant professor at Brown University (attested 2020).
Fiona Ross (born 1954) specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1978–1988) and held posts at Tiro Typeworks and the University of Reading (~2003).

Fitzedward Hall (1825–1901) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer and Harvard. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Sanskrit College, and King's College London, and served as librarian for the India Office (~1862–1869).

Flavio A. Geisshuesler works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Lausanne, Bern, and Virginia, where he completed a PhD under David Germano, and held a postdoctoral research position at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2019.
Flora Blanchon was a scholar who studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she later taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Bucharest, Waseda, and Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, he held professorships at Kansai Medical University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Florinda De Simini (born 1983) is an Indology scholar who held positions at the University of Naples Federico II (~2015–2018) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2019).
Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London from 1967 to 1971 and under Chögyam Trungpa between circa 1971 and 1987.

Francesco Sferra (born 1965) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, having studied under Raffaele Torella. He held posts at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East, University of Naples "L'Orientale", and University of Naples Federico II.
Francis Brinkley (1841–1912) was a specialist in Japanology. He studied at the Royal School Dungannon and held a post at the University of Tokyo from circa 1878 to 1888.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton (1762–1829) studied medicine at Edinburgh under John Hope. Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he served in the Bengal Medical Service and directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

Francis Gladwin (1745–1812) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1806).

Francis H. Cook (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1991) and chaired the Numata Center in 1999.

Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a master's degree in ancient history and pursued doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier at the University of Calicut (attested 2002).
